Restricted cubic spline basis

Source: R/OncReg.other.R
OR.RCS.Rd

Returns the restricted cubic spline basis¹ of x. The first column is x itself and the next k - 2 columns are the nonlinear terms. If x has missing values, an additional column indicates missingness.

Usage

OR.RCS(x, k = 3, knots = NULL, missing.ref = NULL, name = NULL)

Arguments

x

Numeric vector.

k

Number of knots, where k ≥ 3. Ignored if knots is specified. Default = 3.

knots

Optional numeric vector of knot locations. Default = NULL.

missing.ref

Value of x at which the spline columns are evaluated for missing observations, so that the missing indicator compares missing observations with x = missing.ref. Required if x has missing values, otherwise ignored. Default = NULL.

name

Optional string prefixed to the column names. Default = NULL.

Value

Numeric matrix with length(x) rows and one column fewer than the number of knots (named 1, 2, ...), plus a missing-indicator column (named missing) if x has missing values. Knot locations are returned in the "knots" attribute.

Details

Knot locations and the basis are the same as rms::rcs(), except an error is thrown if there are fewer distinct knots than requested.

Missing values are handled differently; rms::rcs() returns NA rows, so observations with missing x are dropped from a subsequent regression. Here, missing observations are assigned the spline columns of x = missing.ref and a column indicating missingness is appended, so that these observations are retained and the indicator compares them with x = missing.ref.

References

  1. Gauthier, J., Wu, Q.V. and Gooley, T.A., 2020. Cubic splines to model relationships between continuous variables and outcomes: a guide for clinicians. Bone Marrow Transplantation, 55(4), pp. 675–680.

See also
